title: Demand notice for structural defects against a developer, four years post-handover

input.text: Client is an allottee, possession 2021, RERA-registered project, registered agreement. Ceiling slab in the living room has a crack that has widened over eight months, and the bathroom waterproofing has failed into the flat below — the neighbour has complained twice to the society. Developer says the defect liability period expired and cites the agreement's 5-year clause but also says 'structural' does not cover waterproofing. Society has issued a notice to our client to repair. Engineer's inspection note attached, photographs, society notices, agreement, possession letter. Client wants a demand notice and then RERA. Draft the demand. Also tell me whether the five-year clause helps or hurts us.

triage.oneLineRead: Live structural risk with a third-party exposure to the flat below. The five-year clause is the client's best asset, not the developer's, and the drafting must pin the defect as structural within that period.

issueMap.issue: Whether a slab crack is a 'structural defect' within the statutory defect-liability provision
issueMap.note: This is the whole case. If the crack is structural, the statutory five-year window applies and the developer's 'expired' answer is wrong.

issueMap.issue: Whether waterproofing failure falls inside or outside the clause
issueMap.note: The developer will argue it is a maintenance item. Engineer's note must be read for causation, not just description.

issueMap.issue: Whether the defect was notified within five years of possession
issueMap.note: Possession 2021, notice 2026 — inside the window if possession is the trigger. Confirm the exact possession date.

issueMap.issue: Whether the client's own liability to the flat below and to the society is running in parallel
issueMap.note: It is, and it creates urgency and a recoverable head of loss.

issueMap.issue: Whether the remedy lies in RERA, a civil suit, or both
issueMap.note: RERA has jurisdiction over the allottee-promoter dispute; the third-party claim against the client is separate. Parallel proceedings risk inconsistent findings.

chronology.event: Waterproofing failure into flat below; two society notices

verification.proposition: Promoter's obligation to rectify structural defects within five years of possession
verification.provision: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act 2016, s. 14(3)
verification.sourceUrlNote: Sub-section number and the proviso on compensation to be confirmed against the bare Act before pleading. Official bare-Act link added.

verification.proposition: Allottee's remedy before the RERA authority
verification.provision: RERA Act 2016, s. 31 read with s. 18
verification.sourceUrlNote: Forum confirmed; relief framing is fact-dependent. Official bare-Act link added.

verification.proposition: Defect liability runs from possession, not from registration
verification.sourceUrlNote: The exact trigger wording matters and is unverified in the fixture.

verification.proposition: Structural defect must be distinguished from ordinary wear

3. Statutory position: the promoter's obligation to rectify structural defects within five years of possession — Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act 2016, s. 14(3). This notice is issued within that window.

terminalOutcome.label: Issue the demand, but pin the defect as structural and within five years on the face of the notice
terminalOutcome.rationale: The statutory window is the client's shield and it is closing. The developer's two arguments — expiry and 'not structural' — are answered by the possession date and the engineer's causation opinion. The notice should not be a general complaint; it should read as a s. 14(3) notice.
terminalOutcome.nextAction: Settle the notice around the possession date and the engineer's causation finding, issue it, and prepare the RERA complaint in parallel for filing on expiry of the notice period.

teachingNotes: The client asks whether the five-year clause helps or hurts. It helps, and enormously — a beginner would read it as the developer's defence. Read the clause as the client's limitation grant, not the developer's escape.

'Structural' is the battleground. The engineer's note is worth more than every photograph if it says why the crack is structural; if it only describes the crack, the notice will be met with 'cosmetic'.
The parallel exposure to the flat below is the urgency. A demand letter that ignores the society notices looks like a grumble; one that annexes them looks like a claim.
The engine blocks the RERA complaint but allows the notice. Correct sequencing: notice first, complaint on expiry. Filing the complaint today hands the developer a notice objection.
commonMistakes: Reading the five-year clause as the developer's defence and advising the client the case is time-barred.
Issuing a general grievance letter with no statutory framing.
Ignoring the society notices so the third-party loss is never quantified.
Filing the RERA complaint before the notice period runs out.
seniorVariants: Frame the notice as a statutory s. 14(3) notice: possession date, defect, engineer's causation opinion, rectification demand, consequential loss, and a stated compliance period.
Put the developer to production of the structural drawings and the slab design, and reserve the right to a joint expert inspection.
Write to the society confirming the client is pursuing the developer, so the client's own position with the society is protected.
Quantify the neighbour's damage and any repair estimate as a separate head, and keep the two claims analytically distinct.

accuracy.adverseFact: If the agreement's defect-liability clause is shorter than five years, the developer will argue contractual restriction. The statutory floor is generally read as non-derogable, but the clause must be read and answered rather than assumed away.
